- Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, often missing upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts overshoot after sharp price increases, then fails to correct.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10–15 days, suggesting lag in adjusting to recent downward trends.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model holds prices too high for too long after peaks.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “tail” of the distribution — especially in the last 5–7 days, where true values frequently rise faster than predicted.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — tends to stick to recent high values even when data suggests a correction is imminent.
- In cases of sustained upward trends, model underestimates the continuation, especially in the final 10 days.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture sudden reversals or sharp drops that occur near the end of the horizon.
